en.title: Lexicographically Smallest Index Permutation for Maximum Information Gain
en.description:
Output a permutation p of 1..n that maximizes sum(i*data[p[i]]), where i and p are both interpreted as 1-based; if several permutations tie, take the lexicographically smallest. The index range 0..n in the original formula is a typo; changing the weights to 0..n−1 only shifts the result by a fixed total and does not affect the optimal permutation.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains data. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, −10^9≤data≤10^9. The output is a permutation of original array indices, not the sorted values or the rank of each element.
en.output: Output n 1-based original indices, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: The answers are 2 3 1, 3 1 2 and 1 3 2. Equal values are ordered by ascending original index.
hints: Sort the original indices by (data[i],i) in ascending order and output them as 1-based indices.
